title: Tiling latency splay - scratchbook
content:
Purpose
Quick personal scratchbook capturing an experiment exploring request tiling/windowing (I call it \"tiling\") as a micro-optimization for tail latency during bursty arrivals. Trying to reason about tradeoffs between per-request latency jitter and sustained throughput when we convexly pack small short requests with long context ones.

Hypothesis
- By slicing long sequences into time-windowed tiles for the runtime scheduler (tile window = X ms), we can reduce queuing-induced tail amplification when spikes cluster.
- Too short a tile window increases packing overhead & KV-cache churn, harming throughput. Too long a window increases p99.

Setup
- Model: open-llama-13b (float16), single-GPU node (A100-80GB) in local private cluster (dev rack).
- Runtime: local dev branch with tiling hook (harper/tiling-explore).
- Quantization: none for these runs (keep deterministic).
- Batch policy baseline: continuous batching with timeout=8ms, max_batch=32.
- Tiling parameter sweep: tile_window_ms = [0 (baseline), 2, 5, 10, 25, 50]
- Request mix: 70% short (<64 tokens), 20% medium (64-256), 10% long (>256) typical webchat workload.
- Arrival pattern: two modes
  * microburst: Poisson background (qps=50) + burst spikes to 850 qps for 1s every 30s
  * ramp: linear ramp 0->600 qps over 120s repeated
- Instrumentation: per-request p50/p90/p95/p99/avg, end-to-end (ingress->response) plus internal queue time, kv-cache-hit boolean, batch_size distribution.

What I changed in code
- Added tiling.window_ms in scheduler config
- When open windows, scheduler groups requests that arrived within same window and forms batches up to max_batch. Windows are non-overlapping, aligned to wall-clock tile boundaries.
- If window expires with no requests, scheduler flushes early. Also added an opt-in per-tenant header to disable tiling.

Raw observations (microburst mode)
- Baseline (tile=0): p50=18ms, p95=72ms, p99=210ms, avg=34ms. Batch sizes concentrated 8-18 during bursts, KV hit ~82%.
- tile=2ms: p50=19ms, p95=68ms, p99=170ms, avg=33ms. Slight p99 improvement, batch sizes slightly larger at peak (10-24). KV hit 78%.
- tile=5ms: p50=21ms, p95=60ms, p99=140ms, avg=32ms. Noticeable p99 drop; more stable tail. Batch sizes 12-28. KV hit 74%.
- tile=10ms: p50=24ms, p95=62ms, p99=150ms, avg=33ms. p50 drifted up; p95 similar; p99 worse than 5ms.
- tile=25ms: p50=31ms, p95=95ms, p99=260ms, avg=40ms. Too long: queues build so burst gets large latency.
- tile=50ms: catastrophic for microbursts: p99 > 450ms, throughput dips when bursts overlap and eviction increases.

Ramp mode observations
- Baseline: smooth ramp, p99 climbs gradually as queueing increases. Tile windows 2-5ms had modest improvements in p99 during steep parts of ramp.
- At sustained high qps (>500), tiling didn't help; batcher already at max throughput and KV churn began to dominate for tile >=10ms.

Interpreting KV-cache impact
- KV cache hit decreased with larger tiles because requests with different contexts got coalesced into batches causing context interleaving and higher cache eviction (we use per-GPU token cache with LRU slice).
- The sweet spot (~5ms) balanced more cohesive packing of near-simultaneous short requests without mixing too much diversity across contexts.

Quick numeric summary (selected)
- microburst p99: baseline 210ms -> tile 5ms 140ms (33% improvement)
- microburst avg latency: baseline 34ms -> tile 5ms 32ms (~6% improvement)
- KV hit: baseline 82% -> tile5ms 74% (tradeoff)
- peak throughput stable across tile windows up to 10ms; >10ms saw evaporation due to KV churn

Notes on batch-size distribution
- With tiling, batch sizes become bursty aligned with tile boundaries. Observed higher variance but higher median batch size during microbursts which reduces per-token runtime overhead.
- Side-effect: scheduling alignment added small wall-clock artifacts (saw micro-step pattern in latency histogram at multiples of tile boundary). Potential for smoothing via jittered window alignment.

Failure modes seen
- Tenant with many long-context requests saw throughput degradation with tiling enabled (tile >=10ms) because long requests occupied slots in tiled batches and reduced short-request prioritization.
- Interleaving contexts increased cache misses; for memory-constrained GPU setups this cascaded to kernel config thrashing (different attention memory patterns) -> slowdown.

Next experiments (TODO)
- Sweep tile_window with jitter: tile_window_ms +/- uniform(0,1ms) to remove wall-clock alignment artifacts.
- Try per-tenant adaptive tiling: measure immediate kv_hit and switch off tiling for tenants with hit<70%.
- Combine tiling with priority lanes: ensure long-context requests are placed in a separate lane that doesn't block short-request tiles.
- Run same sweep with quantized (8-bit) model — see if KV churn penalty smaller or bigger.
- Do A/B test on canary with small % of traffic in staging for 24h to observe real client-mix behavior.

Questions / open points
- What is the right signal to auto-disable tiling? KV-hit? tail latency delta? Both?
- Is there a way to prefetch or pin frequently used context fragments to reduce eviction penalty? (maybe pin top-N per-tenant KV entries)
- Could tiling be implemented at proxy layer with more global view (aggregate across GPUs) vs per-GPU scheduler?

Quick conclusion for now
- Small tile windows (~5ms) improve p99 in highly spiky microburst scenarios for mixed request mixes at our test scale, at the cost of lower KV cache hit. Not a universal win; needs tenant-aware heuristics and priority separation.

Immediate action items (short)
- Implement jittered tile alignment and rerun microburst sweep (assigned to Samir).
- Add per-tenant KV-hit metric to runtime telemetry pipeline (Lina to PR a minor metric).
- Draft a short playbook note for rollouts: default tiling off, enable for tenants exhibiting frequent microbursts with high short-request ratio.

Scratch artifacts
- local perf traces: /mnt/dev-perf/traces/tiling/harper-20251003-*.proto (copied to drive later)
- perf config branch: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/tree/harper/tiling-explore (PR GH-PR-4218)

Random scribbles
- consider hybrid: tile for ingress-proxy to aggregate across clients into short buckets, then hand off to per-GPU scheduler that respects client affinity.
- potential patent? probably too incremental but note: \"request-window packing with eviction-aware pinning\"

End of scratchbook (keep this rough)
